title: Sobhita Dhulipala Channels Mumtaz in a Rs 2.15 Lakh Orange Saree by Arpita Mehta
excerpt: The actor's sindoori orange georgette saree, a playful nod to Mumtaz's iconic Brahmachari look, balances retro Bollywood glamour with contemporary styling.
body:
• Sobhita Dhulipala posted photos in a sindoori orange Arpita Mehta saree, citing Mumtaz's iconic Brahmachari look as inspiration
  • The Sindoori & Rose Gold Hand Embroidered Tiered Sari Set, crafted in georgette, is priced at Rs 2.15 lakh
  • The styling leans into maximalist retro Bollywood glamour — chandelier earrings, stacked bangles, sindoor — while the silhouette remains contemporary

Sobhita Dhulipala has turned a social media post into one of the more interesting fashion moments of the year. The actor shared photos on Instagram wearing a vivid sindoori orange saree by designer Arpita Mehta, accompanied by a caption that was equal parts charming and chaotic: "Inspired by orange wala tang, inspired by that Pinterest photo of Mumtaz in the Mumtaz saree, inspired by the setting Sun, inspired by last night's gaajar halwa in the fridge, inspired by sasuraal genda phool," as reported by Bollywood Hungama.

The Mumtaz Reference, Without the Costume

The most obvious fashion touchstone is Mumtaz's iconic orange saree from Brahmachari (1968) — a look that has been referenced, recreated, and revived countless times across Indian fashion and cinema. What makes Sobhita's version noteworthy is that it borrows the idea without attempting a recreation.

https://x.com/filmimagic/status/2089251345610264592

Where the original Mumtaz look was tightly pleated and body-conscious, this Arpita Mehta saree features a tiered construction that gives the lower half a sculptural quality. The georgette fabric keeps the overall silhouette fluid, while the embroidered rose-gold border creates definition without rigidity. The body of the saree carries small silver-toned motifs against the sheer fabric, with the heavier embellishment concentrated along the borders.

Where the Drama Lives

The blouse does most of the heavy lifting in terms of traditional richness. Covered in dense rose-gold embroidery, it provides visual weight against the comparatively delicate saree. The proportions work precisely because the contrast is deliberate — a heavily embroidered upper half against a fluid lower half, connected by the ornate border running through both.

"Inspired by orange wala tang, inspired by that Pinterest photo of Mumtaz in the Mumtaz saree, inspired by the setting Sun, inspired by last night's gaajar halwa in the fridge, inspired by sasuraal genda phool."

— Sobhita Dhulipala, on Instagram

The jewellery is deliberately maximal. Sobhita wears large chandelier-style earrings with green and pink stone accents, paired with stacked traditional bangles. A visible streak of sindoor adds another traditional detail. The makeup stays polished and warm — defined eyes, sculpted skin, and a muted nude lip — while her hair is pulled back into a neat swept-back style that keeps the face and earrings exposed.

Nostalgia Done Right

The saree is officially described as the Sindoori & Rose Gold Hand Embroidered Tiered Sari Set, priced at Rs 2.15 lakh. It is available through Pernia's Pop Up Shop. But the price tag is less interesting than what the look manages to communicate: warmth, tradition, cinematic glamour, and a playful refusal to take any of it too seriously.

Retro Bollywood references are everywhere in contemporary Indian fashion. The more interesting interpretations tend to borrow a single element rather than reproduce an entire aesthetic. Sobhita's look accomplishes this — recognisably Mumtaz-coded, but filtered through her own styling sensibility and the contemporary construction of Arpita Mehta's design.

What It Signals

Since her wedding to Naga Chaitanya in December 2024, Sobhita has leaned increasingly into traditional Indian fashion — Kanjeevaram silks for the ceremony, temple jewellery for formal appearances, and now a retro-Bollywood inspired saree for what appears to be a more casual outing. The through-line is a commitment to maximalist Indian aesthetics without the minimalist hedging that dominates much of contemporary celebrity styling.
nri_angle: Sobhita Dhulipala's fashion moments consistently resonate with the global Indian diaspora, where traditional saree culture remains a powerful cultural touchstone.
